scope: Twelve canonical Wavefunctions halls, final-text illustrations.

plates.title: RETURNING DIFFERENTLY
plates.subtitle: Introduction
plates.focus: A repeated position omits velocity, accepted release directions and the distinct beginnings kept by counter and prediction.
plates.summary: The bob crosses the same ring in opposite directions. A hand, a prediction and a counter begin at different times.
plates.footer: Two returns that look alike from the doorway answer a push differently.
panels: The ring marks a place the bob keeps leaving.
Visitor beside thin-pivot pendulum, hand releases bob from side; fixed ring marks central rest position. Pale museum, actual material relation of reference. No person beneath swinging hazard.
At the ring the angle is close to zero on both passes.

Two clearly SCHEMATIC temporal insets OUTWARD / RETURN: bob at SAME central ring location, velocity arrows OPPOSITE directions. Single pivot above. Angle 0 in both, velocity sign + / −. These are separate times.
The body can be still for an instant without having finished moving.
Bob displaced at side turning point, small v=0 label, restoring arrow toward centre. No stop/pause control claim. Person watches fleeting hesitation.
A sideways flourish can occupy your hand and contribute little to this number.
Hand gesture arrow has allowed TANGENT component and faint off-plane component. Small projection diagram, no hand making bob leave its swing plane. Same bob and fixed pivot.
The prediction did not watch your hand.
Gold pre-drawn standard prediction curve behind actual larger swing. Tiny schematic labels STANDARD START / YOUR RELEASE; no claimed exact overlay or fitted trajectory.
There are several beginnings here: the engine's, the counter's, the prediction's, the moment you let go.

Wide museum: companion looks at continuing count, adult starts a release. Four small named beginnings as quiet textual sidebar, no fabricated numerical readings. Nearby clocked cube repeats without new push affecting it.
plates.source_review: Temporal insets select separate passes. Standard prediction and visitor release have different initial conditions. Projection sketches are explanatory; drawn arrows and curves do not certify numerical motion or damping.

plates.title: WHERE A SWING LEAVES ITS PAST
plates.subtitle: Pendulum
plates.focus: An age becomes depth; sample budget and age limit keep different histories, while strobe can hide motion.
plates.summary: Teal marks leave the bob and recede along the hall. Coarse sampling buys duration; a chosen rhythm can make a moving bob look still.
plates.footer: It can also make repetition look like stillness.
panels: Behind the bob, something is leaving the room very slowly.
Museum pendulum in frame with teal sampled trail receding perpendicular to swing plane. Visitor follows a single highlighted teal sample; record not physical rope dragged by bob.
The long direction belongs to something the bob did not do.
Side schematic: bob swings only side-to-side, stationary pivot; separate depth arrow AGE along trail into hall. Adult walks BESIDE trail on museum floor, not atop samples.
An old moment is further away.
Same marked sample at EARLIER / LATER positions further along depth, retains same lateral swing-coordinate, not reversing with bob. Label AGE × 0.6 m/s → DEPTH.
We changed which detail was affordable, and gained duration.

FINE / COARSE cropped schematics: fine dense record SHORTER; coarse sparse record LONGER under same max-history window. Marked as selected detail; no exact visible sample counts. Existing COARSE control.
The pendulum carries on from its current angle and speed; this little piece of its accessible past has gone.
Visitor waits beside oldest record mark, two temporal insets PRESENT / REMOVED with same swing continuing, old mark disappears cleanly not fading or removing pendulum.
This can become an instrument for finding repetition.
STROBE label active; moving bob ghost positions (time diagram) beside sparse almost-aligned teal history marks. Record suggests stillness while bob swings. No actual static bob claim.
plates.source_review: The trail is a record given depth, not a route travelled by the bob. Fine/coarse drawings are cropped density/duration comparisons, not exact sample counts. Strobe reveals aliasing without certifying exact alignment. Earlier/later names refer to two views of the same stored sample; it recedes as its age increases. The deletion inset removes the oldest far-end entry.

plates.title: WHAT A WAVE CAN HOLD
plates.subtitle: Sine Space
plates.focus: Static colliding relief and moving noncolliding walls give the same rule different bodily consequences; a fixed x-gap is one chosen measure.
plates.summary: Spheres meet a folded tray. Two walls sway around a passage that guides the eye without stopping the body.
plates.footer: A repeating value has acquired several bodies already.
panels: The landscape has become part of the movement.
Blue folded tray tilted to open outlet, spherical bodies collide with relief. Focus one sphere in hollow, other bodies cropped. Existing RELEASE desk; no claim exact32 inventory.
A place in the landscape has dimensions; so does what arrives there.

Two clearly schematic separate trials SAME RELIEF, small vs large single sphere at same hollow. Different fit/contact; not simultaneous size transform. SIZE control visible. No guaranteed outcome arrows.
A body present at this deadline has not been proven permanently trapped.

End-window diagram 12 s, one body STILL IN, departed bodies moved to neat record row below. Label REMOVED FROM COLLISIONS at recorded bodies; no invisible eternity proof or continuing active rolling after deadline.
A shape can come to meet a body through its own motion or through the body's movement.
Magenta translucent wavy corridor. RUN: visitor stands while folds move; FREEZE: adult walks beside held folds. Temporal panels within small inset, same floor support.
We have made a constant width by deciding how to measure it.

Half-turn phase setting, both walls swerve same way. Top-view schematic TWO parallel-offset sinusoidal traces, horizontal x-gap arrow exactly across matching longitudinal address, label x-gap. A faint shorter diagonal distinguishes another direction, no numeric width certification.
Their influence did not wait for collision to be enabled.

Adult calmly walks across a translucent magenta wall fold, body partly through visible mesh, foot on thin continuous floor slab. Companion stays in apparent passage. Label WALL: NO COLLISION / FLOOR: SUPPORT; no fall, no solid wall trapping body.
plates.source_review: Tray contact differs from corridor appearance: only the tray supplies a collision surface. Size/relief trial sketches are comparisons, not guaranteed outcomes. The gap inset names its axis; it does not certify shortest clear width.

plates.title: A CIRCLE BECOMING A GRAPH
plates.subtitle: Unit Circle
plates.focus: Sine and cosine project an angular state; one height is ambiguous, two coordinates recover position, and graph progression is not floor travel.
plates.summary: A turning point leaves a graph beside a circle. A repeated height belongs to two different moments.
plates.footer: A beginning is needed to label the progression, even though the circle itself has no privileged first point.
panels: How can going round a circle make a line that rises and falls?

Visitor beside complete rainbow bead circle per reference with bright current point TOP and white projection rods; nearby finite graph starts rising/falling. Adults observing not touching unsupported graph.
The two projections do not reach their extremes together: when one is at an extreme, the other passes through its middle.
Small accurate circle diagram: point TOP at (x=0,y=1), vertical rod length1, horizontal offset0. Separate at RIGHT (x=1,y=0), roles exchange; label TWO MOMENTS. No falsely same extreme.
You have changed where you begin describing the cycle without changing its order.
Four cardinal reference markers RIGHT, TOP, LEFT, BOTTOM around single ring; two small START HERE pointers at different cardinal positions, same cyclic arrow. Point not moved by visitor control.
The graph is not the path the point takes across the floor; its horizontal direction has a different meaning from the circle's horizontal coordinate.
Circle and sine graph beside each other: graph horizontal arrow ANGLE PROGRESSION, vertical HEIGHT; ring centre's horizontal arrow x separately. No walkway or person standing on graph.
Knowing the height therefore does not recover the whole angular position.

Single circle, two dotted explanatory positions upper-right and upper-left SAME y with connecting horizontal dashed line, one rising one falling. Both marker points above centre, not top or opposed ends. Label SAME HEIGHT / DIFFERENT ANGLE.
The point returns to the top; no new step arrives.
Wide circle turning while adjacent graph has completed TWO cycles and stays. Label KEPT GRAPH / POINT CONTINUES. Adults pause at diagram rather than climb it.
plates.source_review: Multiple circle positions are explanatory moments, not additional live points. The graph's angle axis differs from spatial x. The finite drawn graph is not shown as a certified walkable bridge.

plates.title: THE MOTION THAT TRAVELS
plates.subtitle: Wave Propagation
plates.focus: Neighbour forces transmit vertical disturbances through fixed horizontal places; boundaries and reset conditions enter the comparison.
plates.summary: One sphere rises while a disturbance reaches its neighbours. Disconnecting the links keeps the places and changes what can travel.
plates.footer: A boundary is therefore part of the mechanism, not merely where the picture happens to stop.
panels: How can a disturbance travel while its parts stay near their places?
Adult at edge of cropped blue-sphere horizontal grid in museum, red centre drive. One tracked blue neighbour marked quietly, no balls travelling across grid.
The spheres remain at their horizontal grid positions.
Schematic tracked sphere at same horizontal address in LOW / HIGH poses connected by VERTICAL arrow only. Pattern arrow across row distinct and dashed, no horizontal drift of sphere.
Similar heights at one instant do not establish that the two places are always moving together; watch which way each moves next.
Two blue neighbouring sphere snapshots same height, next-direction arrows one UP one DOWN, each above own fixed footprint. No exact measured states claim, label SCHEMATIC RELATION.
Every button restarts the comparison; it does not cut a moving wave midway.

Existing panel PULSE and COUPLED/INDEPENDENT. Two schematic runs start SAME STILL GRID: COUPLED later neighbours displaced; INDEPENDENT centre displaced but neighbours remain level. Clearly RESET THEN DRIVE, not live disconnection at one instant.
An edge cell has fewer neighbours.
Simple grid detail corner sphere TWO links, interior sphere FOUR orthogonal links, no diagonal or wrapped edge links. Whole display cropped; not exact lattice count.
Neither requires the spheres to agree consciously or to know the pattern they collectively form.
Wide quiet view adults attend to spatial pattern with individually vertical sphere positions. No anthropomorphic faces, telepathic links or unimplemented selective-neighbour control.
plates.source_review: Linked/unlinked views describe separate restarted trials. Sphere trajectories are vertical; the moving pattern is relational. Boundary inset selects an orthogonal grid detail, not a full inventory or numerical response. The drawn stems make vertical addresses legible; they do not certify a physical supporting mechanism.

plates.title: ONE WAVE INSIDE ANOTHER
plates.subtitle: Effect Sound
plates.focus: The modulator enters a carrier's phase, with its own decay; keeping a reference and display normalization alter comparison.
plates.summary: A blue carrier waits while an orange control changes the note. What the ear hears need not grow in proportion to its displayed cause.
plates.footer: The rig reports changed parameters, but there is no field in its list for the difference that made you want to listen again.
panels: Begin with one note.
Blue carrier ball and orange modulator ball in SEPARATE open cages atop two desks; adults near instrument. BASELINE and HOLD available, scope above. Reference shapes only, no debug HUD.
You do not have to keep the first sound intact in memory.
Adult presses COMPARE; small timeline A / GAP / B, A held vs current B. Blue ball unmoved; orange a little higher. Label differs: I only, no fabricated exactvalues.
The orange contribution is not mixed in as a second audible output.
Small rule 'sin(carrier phase + modulator) × carrier envelope'. Orange arrow enters INSIDE sine phase brackets; envelope sits outside. No A+B mixing diagram or two-speaker output.
Something we first heard as one fading has separated into two processes we can vary.
Two distinct labelled schematic decay envelopes CARRIER and MODULATOR; orange depth arrow over desk changes MODULATOR DECAY, blue unchanged. No one decay asserted controls both.
A setting that would spoil one imitation may be the beginning of another sound.
Adult listens while moving orange left-right, label RATIO, no branded instrument likeness or historical figure. Companion gives ear attention; small no numeric observation.
The output changes while the apparent height of its cause can stay much the same.

Scope selected-detail: orange normalized lane same-height before/after I change, output trace different. Label NORMALIZED MODULATOR LANE / OUTPUT. Not whole-note envelope, small 'near attack' note. Keep one same orange control.
plates.source_review: The orange signal changes phase rather than becoming a second mixed output. Scope traces are schematic, normalized and cropped near attack; they do not depict an entire note or certify calibrated audio levels.

plates.title: A MOVEMENT KEPT IN A COLUMN
plates.subtitle: Bernini
plates.focus: Twist through height differs from whole-object rotation through time; arrangement and authored audio contribute separately.
plates.summary: A pale twisting shaft offers two readings. Follow a ridge upward, then wait for the solid to turn past you.
plates.footer: Watching that rotation does not explain how the twist was made, and following the twist does not require the column to rotate.
panels: Can a shape keep the rhythm of a movement without travelling along it?
Adult and companion enter high warm-marble twisting colonnade, repeated sculptural shafts. Sober pale museum with dramatic calm light, no literal Vatican/history reenactment.
Choose one ridge on a twisting shaft and follow it upward.
Adult gazes up following one subtle highlighted helical ridge, arrow HEIGHT upward. One continuous twisted column fixed central axis, human on floor.
This second observation follows change through time.
Two schematic times at SAME HEIGHT: column cross-section rotates as whole, TIME arrow, not column stretching or ridge travelling vertically.
The form and its arrangement contribute different things: one supplies the twist, the other decides whether you meet a field of objects, a threshold or an aisle.

Wide repeated current colonnade view with sightline through gaps. Small conceptual silhouettes FIELD / THRESHOLD / AISLE explicitly possibilities, no arrangement control or claim this version switches.
Touching a shaft does not play it.
Hand resting near shaft, separate low HUM label with ROTATION SPEED relation. No magical touch sparks, no playable vibrating notes caused by finger.
Which “now” has the repeated phrase brought back?
Adult pauses by separate wall voice instrument labelled 'right here, right now', column keeps rotating in background. Small repeat arrow around phrase, not words spoken by column or protagonist.
plates.source_review: Spatial twist, whole-object rotation and separate voice playback are different constructions. The repeated set is selected from the chapter, not a newly implemented rearrangement lesson. Architectural resemblance is not a documented influence or historical reconstruction.
